newsitem.title: USA: No cold threat seen to Brazil coffee - Smith Barney.
newsitem.headline: No cold threat seen to Brazil coffee - Smith Barney.

text.p: A cold airmass which brought chilly temperatures to Brazil's coffee belt this past weekend is expected to move out into the Atlantic and bring in warmer weather during the next week, said Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis.

As a result, Davis said in his daily update that low temperatures on Tuesday in Brazil's coffee-growing regions would primarily be in the lower 40s to the lower 50s F (5-12 C). Lows during the middle to the end of the week will be in the 50s and lower 60s F, he said.

"In fact, during the next week there is no indication of any significant cold airmasses moving up into Brazil from Argentina," Davis stated. "Thus, there is no threat of any frost/freeze damage during the next week in Brazil."
Forecasters in Brazil are anticipating colder temperatures for the country's coffee belt, but said any frosts are expected to be limited to lower-lying areas where coffee is not grown.
National Institute of Meteorology (Inmet) forecastes a repeat of last night's chilly weather, with minimum temperatures expected to be around two to three degrees Celsius (37 F).
